sections.markdown:
## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Stopped vehicles and warning lights

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A02
Violating the stopped-vehicle warning-light law described in South Dakota Codified Law 32-31-6.1 is classified as a Class 2 misdemeanor. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A02
The handbook says a Class 2 misdemeanor for violating its stopped-vehicle warning-light rule can be punished by a fine, county-jail time, or both. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A02
Under South Dakota Codified Law 32-31-6.2, causing a crash while violating 32-31-6.1 is a Class 1 misdemeanor when the crash involves a stopped emergency vehicle using red signals or any stopped vehicle using amber, yellow or blue warning lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]
